Untouched by the hands of time and fed by both the ocean and warm fresh water springs, Ridback Bay is teeming with sea life. A remote, timeless bayside village is now being inundated by entrepreneurs awaiting the influx of the world's greatest fisherman to harvest this plentiful bounty. The docks and warehouses are being revitalized and now it is time to begin the real adventure. Go build your fleet and become the master of the seas! Fleet was the 2012 Dice Hate Me Game of the Year, and a runner up for GAMES Magazine's 2014 Best Card Game of the Year. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Fleet is a card game where players seek the most victory points by purchasing fishing licenses, launching boats, and hiring captains to gather fish. Contents 1 Gameplay 1.1 Phase One: License Auction 1.2 Phase Two: Launch Boats and Hire Captains 1.3 Phase Three: Fishing 1.4 Phase Four: Processing and Trading 1.5 Phase Five: Draw 2 Game End 2.1 Conditions 2.2 Scoring 3 Boat Cards 4 License Cards 4.1 Shrimp License 4.2 Cod License 4.3 Lobster License 4.4 Tuna License 4.5 Processing Vessel License 4.6 Fishermen's Pub 4.7 King Crab License 5 Gone Fishin' Gameplay The game is played in rounds of five phases each. Each phase is played in turn order. At the end of a round the starting player token is passed to the next player and a new round begins. Phase One: License Auction Players may purchase a fishing license from the license auction, using the boat cards from their hand as cash. Other players may attempt to out bid each other. The license is then placed in front of the winner. Phase Two: Launch Boats and Hire Captains Players may launch a boat from their hand (matching a fishing license they own) by selecting it and paying (discarding) the launch cost using other boat cards from their hand as cash. Players may then hire a captain by placing a boat card from their hand face down on any of their available launched boats. Phase Three: Fishing Players gain a crate of fish from the supply on each of their captained boats that is not already at capacity (4). Phase Four: Processing and Trading If able, a player may process one crate of fish per boat for later use. A player may then trade one crate of fish from their processed supply for a boat card. Phase Five: Draw Players draw two cards and discard one of the cards just drawn. Game End Conditions The game ends when either there are not enough license cards to completely refill the auction after Phase One, or the supply of fish crates runs out during Phase Three In either case the game will end after Phase Three of that round. If the fish crates run out, all players still receive credit for fish crates due to them. Scoring At the end of the game players score Victory Points (VP): +VP for all purchased license cards +VP for all launched boats +1VP for each fish crate on launched boats ( not processed) Bonus VP from King Crab licenses +2VP for each Gone Fishin' card in hand (if applicable) The player with the most VP wins. If tied, the player with the most launched boats wins. If still tied, then the player with the most fish crates on boats wins. Boat Cards Boat cards in a player's hand can be used in many ways. They can be discarded as money, launched as a boat, or played upside down as a captain. The money value is shown as a number of coins in the bottom left. The cost to launch and victory points earned are shown in the upper left and right, respectively. And any boat can be used to captain any other boat. The deck includes 20 of each Shrimp, Lobster, and Processing Vessel and 12 of each Cod, Tuna, and King Crab. License Cards Each fishing license not only allows a player to launch that type of boat, but it also provides a special bonus. These bonuses improve as players acquire additional copies of a license. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] My friends and I tried to play this game but were never able to figure out how to get it moving properly.  We contacted the designer, but his vague description on how the game worked left us more perplexed than enlightened.  Since we could never get anywhere near where someone could win the game, we finally gave up and wrote the whole thing off as a non-starter. I contributed to the fund raiser for the Arctic Bounty expansion, which means I have a even more stuff I need to put up on eBay to sell, completely untouched.

[Rating: 1/10] This was a horrid game to try and play. Couldn't comprehend how to make it work but we had the dice game and that was a much better version!

[Rating: 2/10] Thin theme and tight money system rewards lucky draws and once a leader always a leader.

[Rating: 2/10] First turn seemed too important... Want to try again but getting behind is horrible.  -- 8 years later --  Played again. Not very good. Dull, dull, dull...  -- and another 2 years later --   Still BAD!!

[Rating: 2/10] This is very very similar to just the auction part of Outpost. Amazingly, it actually is a worse version of Outpost (which is a pretty bad game) because it amplifies the run away leader problem that plagues Outpost. It doesn't really have a mitigating factor of loss of factory building to compensate for the loss of a key bid.  There are easily situations where the first player can just win if for instance they get a Tuna boat turn one and all the other boats offered are processing or shrimp.   Also, like Outpost, the game isn't particularly fun to play, while you're playing it.

[Rating: 2.8/10] I don't think I have played a game that had a worse disconnect between theme and mechanics.

[Rating: 3/10] Played this game over the weekend and played with kickstarter stuff. The KS stuff seemed over powered and might be the cause for the game being so bad. Sometimes you have to sit for 3 plus turns just waiting to build money to make a purchase which is a bad thing. You sit down to play a game not pass pass pass. The weather advisory card ruins the already broken mechanic of richer get richer in this game.

[Rating: 3/10] This game fails for me in every single way as a two player game, which is annoying. I hear there's a 2p variant somewhere, I'll try that.

[Rating: 3/10] My friend feels we must have been playing some rules wrong (the rules are not well written), but I couldn't find any errors.  The game seems just totally dry and kind of pointless. I have not idea what the hype is about - I would always prefer San Juan or Race over this one.  The auctions for licenses are not fun, since you rarely have much money to bid high, and are guaranteed a license, so what's the point of bidding high.  And the theme is not that prevalent - I don't feel like I'm going out to sea to get fish.

[Rating: 3/10] A clone of San Juan/Race to the Galaxy. The added auction mechanism is not convincing. The theme is not consistent (i have to leave fish on the boat? what are 'processing vessels'?). As a strategic game, it is disappointing. For a family game, it is too dry and complicated. The game design does not address the inherent problem of early advantage-victories.

[Rating: 3/10] Tthis is not my favorite game, the system rewards lucky draws and it bored the whole time. I was very disappointed so .... never again

[Rating: 3/10] 2 / 5 - Fair  It passes time. Confused as to what it offers that other games don't already do better. Except shrimp, possibly.

[Rating: 3/10] Passes the point of being too tight and just being unwelcome. It felt as if there was a very limited number of strategies.
